short_name: NRC Protection of digital computer and communication systems and networks
summary: Licensees must provide high assurance that digital assets supporting safety, important-to-safety, security, emergency preparedness and support functions are protected against cyber attacks up to the design basis threat, via an NRC-approved cyber security plan and program.
applies_to: Nuclear power reactor licensees (10 CFR Part 50 operating licenses and Part 52 combined licenses).
status: In effect; guidance RG 5.71 Rev. 1 (Feb. 2023). NRC has EO 14300-driven proposed rules pending (Jul. 16, 2026 and Sep. 24, 2026) whose cyber impact was not verified.

summary: Consequence-based cybersecurity program for commercial nuclear plants licensed under Part 53 that elect this section; guidance RG 5.96 Rev. 0 (Mar. 2026).
size_thresholds: Graded by potential consequences (offsite dose thresholds in 10 CFR 53.210).
status: Part 53 final rule effective Apr. 29, 2026 (FR 2026-06048, Mar. 30, 2026).

summary: Tiered notification and 24-hour recordkeeping of cyber attacks and related events for 73.54/73.110 licensees.

short_name: NERC CIP Reliability Standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014; CIP-015 approved)
citation: Federal Power Act sec. 215 (16 U.S.C. 824o); 18 CFR Part 40; NERC CIP-002-5.1a, CIP-003-9, CIP-004 to CIP-014 (current enforceable versions)
summary: Mandatory cyber and physical security standards for BES Cyber Systems: categorization, security management, personnel, ESPs, physical security, system security, incident response/reporting, recovery, configuration/vulnerability management, information protection, supply chain, and physical security of transmission.
applies_to: NERC-registered entities (Balancing Authorities, Distribution Providers meeting criteria, Generator Owners/Operators, Reliability Coordinators, Transmission Owners/Operators) owning BES Cyber Systems.
size_thresholds: Impact rating via CIP-002 Attachment 1 bright-line criteria, e.g., medium impact for generation with net Real Power capability >= 1,500 MW in a single Interconnection; high impact for control centers of BA/GOP/TOP controlling >= 3,000 MW; UFLS/UVLS programs of 300 MW or more bring Distribution Providers into scope. Low-impact assets have reduced (CIP-003) requirements.
status: CIP-003-9 (vendor remote access for low impact) effective Apr. 1, 2026. Future U.S. effective dates per NERC bulletin (Aug. 31-Sep. 7, 2026): virtualization revisions CIP-002-8, CIP-003-10, CIP-004-8, CIP-005-8, CIP-006-7.1, CIP-007-7.1, CIP-008-7.1, CIP-009-7.1, CIP-010-5, CIP-011-4.1, CIP-013-3 on July 1, 2028 (FERC Order No. 919, eff. May 26, 2026); CIP-015-1 INSM on Oct. 1, 2028 (FERC approved, eff. Sep. 2, 2025); CIP-003-11 on July 1, 2029 (FERC Order No. 918); CIP-015-2 on Oct. 1, 2029. FERC directed further supply-chain revisions (final action eff. Nov. 24, 2025).

short_name: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024)
summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours, and preserve related data.
applies_to: Entities in a critical infrastructure sector that exceed the SBA small-business size standard for their NAICS code, or meet a sector-based criterion. Sector criterion: owns/operates a commercial nuclear power reactor or fuel cycle facility licensed by NRC.
size_thresholds: Proposed 226.2(a): exceeds SBA size standard in 13 CFR Part 121 for the entity's NAICS code (employee- or revenue-based depending on NAICS); sector-based criteria apply regardless of size.
status: NOT YET IN EFFECT. NPRM published Apr. 4, 2024; comment period closed Jul. 3, 2024; CISA held additional town halls in 2026 (FR notices Feb. 13, 2026 and May 26, 2026) on scope and burden. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda projected the final rule for 09/2026; no final rule found in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Reporting obligations begin only on the final rule's effective date.
